# Temple Scroll Column 45 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 45 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**45:1** Among the birds, consider these unclean — do not eat them, for they are detestable: the eagle, the vulture, and the osprey.

**45:2** The kite and every kind of falcon.

**45:3** Every kind of raven.

**45:4** The ostrich, the nighthawk, the sea gull, and every kind of hawk.

**45:5** The little owl, the fishing owl, and the screech owl.

**45:6** The barn owl and every kind of desert owl; every kind of raven.

**45:7** The white owl, the pelican, and the carrion vulture.

**45:8** The stork and every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.

**45:9** All winged insects that swarm are unclean to you — do not eat them.

**45:10** You may eat any clean bird.

**45:11** When a man makes a vow to the LORD or takes an oath that binds him to a commitment, he must not go back on his word.

**45:12** He must do everything he has promised.

**45:13** When a man makes a vow to the LORD, he must not put off fulfilling it. The LORD your God will certainly hold you accountable, and you will bear guilt.

**45:14** But if you choose not to make vows, you will not be guilty.

**45:15** Whatever you have promised with your own mouth, you must keep and carry out, just as you voluntarily vowed to the LORD your God — the freewill offering you pledged to give.

**45:16** For the LORD holds every person accountable for his vows and oaths, and no one may treat his spoken word lightly.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column covers two topics: forbidden birds and the binding nature of vows. The bird list defies precise identification — many ancient Hebrew bird names have no certain modern equivalent. The vow section makes a powerful point: words matter. Once spoken to God, a vow becomes as binding as a law. The one escape clause is simple — don't make vows in the first place (v. 14).*
